batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 candidate IDs and their supplied premeasurement predictions together. Prioritize endpoint-specific failure repair, matched amount and solvent-ratio contrasts, and three targeted repeats that distinguish condition relationships from within-tuple variability. Explore predicted early-ratio maxima in neutral aromatic ethers. Treat quantile widths and CW distance as secondary signals, without assuming calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: m118, pure EA, 150 uL: predicted 5.55/10.55 mL. Recent 1/1 observation 966254b5be3c8ec5edd3 measured 5.32/41.55, whereas matched-amount 2/1 observation 4e7e45a513ce579c5ce3 finished at 12.63. This boundary measurement tests whether broad completion extends toward pure EA or is localized near the surprising row.

m118, pure EA, 50 uL, pairs with the selected 150-uL point despite almost identical predictions. It tests whether any boundary completion expansion depends on amount. The inconsistent-looking low-amount 10/1 observation 2cc254396123c76b9a13 cautions against transferring a single unusual label across this graph's condition surface.

m4, 2/1, 50 uL, supplies the amount contrast to recent 150-uL observation 032d9fbb133dff53e005, measured at 4.18/19.73. At 1/1, 05532ff0857a33a604d0 and 9aadc8feed825d13a5d7 already differ substantially in completion across amount. This tests whether that association persists at 2/1.

m4, 1/1, 100 uL, bridges measured 50- and 150-uL completions of 12.52 and 18.51 in 05532ff0857a33a604d0 and 9aadc8feed825d13a5d7. Its 14.13-mL completion prediction tests interpolation where the model still represents amount contrasts weakly.

m4, 5/1, 150 uL: the predicted completion is 12.59 mL, below measured 1/1 and 2/1 completions of 18.51 and 19.73 in 9aadc8feed825d13a5d7 and 032d9fbb133dff53e005. This tests whether a completion decrease actually occurs farther along the ratio curve after the previously predicted 2/1 trough failed.

m4, pure EA, 150 uL, closes the boundary contrast against measured 1/1 row 9aadc8feed825d13a5d7 and low-amount pure-EA row ef2fd58510bc9f4386a5. The 11.38-mL completion prediction tests whether the high-amount expansion disappears at the strongest eluent or remains underrepresented.

m28, 1/1, 150 uL, extends the matched-ratio amount series from 686562279e2bfb73ef1e and 0d18f3f10c8377d12316, with completions of 12.50 and 18.71 at 50 and 100 uL. It tests completion growth separately from onset, complementing the 5/1 amount contrast in bfbe491a54086b98874d and 050e2fab4b407ea058cb.

m19, 1/1, 50 uL, tests whether the strong onset-versus-amount association established at 2/1 by 6d21e9ec887b3408c612, 304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07 and 906bd247e050658f99d8 persists in stronger eluent. Together with the selected high-amount point and measured 100-uL row 9a60cb4735780275034e, it defines a complete local amount series.

m19, 1/1, 150 uL, completes the selected amount contrast. The model predicts essentially the same endpoints as at 50 uL, while measured 2/1 onsets fall markedly with increasing amount. This discriminates a regime-dependent loading association from a response that transfers across adjacent ratios.

m72, 1/1, 100 uL, PE 300-uL loading, matches measured DCM 200-uL row d90d024730eb01bff3c7 in molecule, ratio and amount. Recent low-amount protocol observations 6a53fc46345dc50021ae and d2472f692763fd970d64 differed despite nearly identical predictions. This tests whether that joint protocol difference reproduces at another amount.

Repeat the m72, 1/1, 50-uL, DCM 200-uL tuple. Observation 6a53fc46345dc50021ae measured 3.53/10.60, substantially earlier than the 100- and 150-uL DCM rows d90d024730eb01bff3c7 and 017b0f98188f8ff58935. A repeat directly tests whether the low-amount endpoint shift is reproducible before teaching a protocol interaction.

Repeat m184 in pure EA at 100 uL. Observation 588b182228e5400a3c7a measured 5.59/9.81, below both 50-uL row 2490762d0471bbb9cc9f and 150-uL row 8435ac7ac5c9c8c37de2. This is the most direct available test of a nonmonotonic amount feature versus within-tuple variability.

m123, pure EA, 50 uL, anchors a fixed-amount three-ratio experiment. The predicted completion is 8.17 mL, compared with 21.09 at selected 1/1 and 11.27 at selected 2/1. Measuring the boundary helps determine whether the predicted early-ratio maximum is reproducible.

m123, 1/1, 50 uL, targets the predicted 21.09-mL completion maximum and the highest supplied CW distance. Existing same-amount weak-eluent observation 832eaa9c6b2f7a68f2a5 finished at 23.16. The selected neighboring ratios make this a response-shape test rather than acquisition based on distance alone.

m123, 2/1, 50 uL, tests the predicted completion decrease after 1/1 while holding amount and loading protocol fixed. Together with the selected pure-EA and 1/1 labels, it can expose an interpolation artifact or teach a genuine endpoint-specific reversal in a neutral aromatic diether.

m126, 1/1, 100 uL, tests whether the analogous predicted completion maximum transfers from dimethoxybenzene m123 to anisole. Its 13.66-mL prediction exceeds matched-amount 2/1 observation 0f694957922ad0e10db2, measured at 8.98. This provides a structural comparison with only one additional label.

m91, 2/1, 50 uL, changes only ratio from recent 1/1 observation fa59cd65f3b5f04bd6af, measured at 7.80/11.80 after completion was underpredicted by 4.63 mL at acquisition. It separates solvent-response curvature from the amount confounding in existing 100-uL observations 02ddeed8a16d3adf3e28 and d603d4af5fd62fa8b85e.

m182, 1/1, 150 uL, tests the transition from recent pure-EA observation 9948433906d4afa41345, which finished at 20.41. Low-amount 1/1 row 52b474514f1e9ba6c4d2 finished at 11.80. This distinguishes a boundary reversal shared across amounts from an amount-associated completion difference.

m131, 2/1, 150 uL, extends the matched-amount early-ratio sequence from pure-EA row 6ddb6596285d680135c6 and recent 1/1 row a78f7bae6726f8eb382a. Paired with the selected diphenylmethane experiment, it tests how a diaryl carbonyl environment changes completion growth without assuming a universal aromatic correction.

m214, 2/1, 150 uL, follows recent 1/1 observation 06906310911a5a7509dd, measured at 4.32/7.72 after acquisition-time completion overprediction of 4.25 mL. Its 9.58-mL completion prediction tests whether the early response persists and supplies a non-carbonyl comparison to m131.

m95, 1/1, 50 uL, brackets measured pure-EA row 9546040e1980860a8fe1 and 2/1 row 8d018e521e8e6bbc53c2. The latter's onset is much later than at higher amounts. This tests where methyl acetoacetate develops its amount-associated onset differences.

m95, 1/1, 100 uL, pairs with the selected 50-uL point despite nearly identical predictions. Measured 2/1 rows 8d018e521e8e6bbc53c2 and 8b6fc534edc07d5b79be differ in both endpoints across these amounts. The pair tests whether that relationship already appears at 1/1.

m45, 5/1, 50 uL, starts a matched amount contrast for the carboxylic-acid context. At 20/1, b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1 and 53a9a2469f8d4ead8732 show substantially earlier onset at greater amount. This interior ratio tests where the association emerges, away from the invalid-order 50/1 record 129036e0bccc4ff7e848.

m45, 5/1, 150 uL, completes the acid amount contrast. Its predicted endpoints are essentially identical to the selected 50-uL point. The labels test whether the clear 20/1 amount association is regime-specific and provide a comparison to neutral and basic loading-response experiments.

m87, 1/1, 100 uL, fills the early-ratio gap between measured pure-EA row 933e17d426dc7efc96b5 and 2/1 row 981a11d7d65c8e5597f9. This methoxybenzoate comparison helps determine whether the unusual m118 aldehyde completion reflects functional-group context rather than a broad methoxy-aromatic adjustment.

m115, 1/1, 50 uL, completes an amount extension of the methoxyacetophenone boundary. Measured 100- and 150-uL rows 352465f62eba993148ee and aa4c0f940c011630a345 have similar completions but different onsets. This tests endpoint-specific amount transfer alongside the methoxybenzaldehyde and methoxybenzoate experiments.

m81, 1/1, 150 uL, adds an early-ratio anchor for an aromatic beta-ketoester. Matched-amount 2/1 observation bee82d193ec1ce4fde27 finished at 7.93, while pure-EA and later-ratio observations can be broader. This tests a possible local contraction and contrasts aromatic beta-ketoester behavior with selected aliphatic m95.

Repeat m81, 2/1, 150 uL, to assess the short completion in bee82d193ec1ce4fde27. Same-tuple 5/1 observations a9500e468002e41eceeb and 5879dc8ccb560446d54c differ markedly in completion, so reproducibility matters before interpreting the selected 1/1-to-2/1 contrast as a response feature.

m138, 1/1, 150 uL, adds an amount contrast to recent low-amount row 9329c6709a6b676368cf. At 2/1, b2717fe0c14d406893ef and d32673e3284e67755674 have similar completions but different onsets. This tests whether that endpoint split extends to the neighboring ratio in a halogenated aromatic.

m60, 1/1, 50 uL, fills a fixed-amount curve between pure-EA behavior and measured 2/1 row c9ad01493d938f825117. Together with 5/1 row 985361f6699d97f9464f and 10/1 row beda2205eedbe1688e1f, it constrains where retention begins to grow in a secondary alcohol.

m67, 1/1, 50 uL, provides a comparison to selected m60 with the hydroxyl group adjacent to the phenyl ring. Measured m67 rows db5dcc7b864e0174fcbd and 2cf4f6424b85ab121943 establish later-ratio retention, while 6125098643b6e16e10e3 is only a prediction. This label tests early-ratio structural transfer without treating that candidate as evidence.

m20, 2/1, 50 uL, tests a neutral ether-containing acrylate against measured high-amount row 65e1a58ab8e4aa2f1eb6. Comparing this contrast with the strong m19 tertiary-amine acrylate amount association tests whether loading-response learning transfers across closely related ester scaffolds with different heteroatom environments.

hypotheses.content: Early-ratio completion responses depend on molecular graph and amount, and can differ from onset responses. Broad m4 and pure-EA m182 intervals coexist with early m214 behavior; a uniform upward correction for aromatic or hydrophobic compounds would erase useful distinctions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local ratio measurements can teach separate V1 and V2 relationships and prevent failure repair in one graph from producing systematic errors in related compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does high-amount m4 completion remain broad in pure EA and at 5/1, and do matched-amount m182, m131 and m214 measurements retain their distinct early-ratio response shapes?

hypotheses.content: Amount associations vary by graph, solvent regime and endpoint. The m19 onset decreases strongly with increasing amount at 2/1, while m4 and m28 show completion growth near 1/1. These observed associations do not establish a universal or causal loading law.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many candidate predictions are nearly invariant across amount. Matched contrasts can teach when onset, completion or both change, and when a relationship fails to transfer to a neighboring ratio or functional-group context.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which amount associations persist at earlier ratios across the tertiary-amine acrylate, neutral beta-ketoester, acid, fused aromatic and methoxy-carbonyl contexts?

hypotheses.content: The unusually broad m118 interval at 1/1 and 150 uL may reflect a localized structure-condition relationship or a variable record. Its extension toward pure EA remains untested and should be established before spreading a large completion correction across methoxy-aromatic compounds.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest acquisition-time V2 error was about 29 mL with relatively accurate onset. Boundary labels and related functional-group comparisons can constrain whether repair should be localized to completion, amount and ratio.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are pure-EA m118 completions ordinary at both selected amounts, or does a broad interval reproduce at the boundary, and how does the early methoxybenzoate response compare?

hypotheses.content: Joint loading-solvent identity and volume differences may matter for m72 near 1/1, but their effect may depend on amount and ratio and remains entangled with within-tuple variability.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor gives almost identical endpoints to the two protocols. A repeat and a matched contrast at another amount can distinguish an overlooked recorded relationship from a localized variable result. The design does not isolate solvent identity from loading-solvent volume.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the early DCM-loaded 50-uL result reproduce, and does PE versus DCM loading produce a corresponding difference at 100 uL and 1/1?

hypotheses.content: The predicted V2 maxima near 1/1 for neutral aromatic ethers m123 and m126 could be reproducible solvent-response features or interpolation artifacts. The supplied widths do not determine which explanation is correct.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A fixed-amount ratio triplet tests response shape directly, while the anisole measurement tests transfer to a simpler graph. These labels cover ordinary neutral chemistry where surprising predictions could otherwise remain unchallenged.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m123 completion rise from pure EA to 1/1 and then fall at 2/1, and does anisole show a similar excess over its measured 2/1 completion?

hypotheses.content: The pure-EA m184 response at 100 uL is lower than at both 50 and 150 uL. This may be a reproducible nonmonotonic amount relationship or within-tuple variability; smooth amount interpolation is currently unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A targeted repeat can prevent a single low result from becoming an unjustified amount feature or, if reproduced, provide evidence for a graph-specific departure from smooth interpolation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does another eligible record at the same 100-uL pure-EA tuple reproduce the earlier onset and completion?

feedback_interpretation: The latest labels strengthen conditional, endpoint-specific reasoning. For m4, the predicted 2/1 completion trough at 150 uL failed: 032d9fbb133dff53e005 finished at 19.73 mL, slightly later than the 18.51-mL 1/1 result. The new 50-uL 1/1 completion of 12.52 supports an amount-associated expansion, so the next measurements separate amount interpolation from ratio curvature. For m19, 6d21e9ec887b3408c612 strongly supports earlier onset with greater amount at 2/1, but the three completions are approximately 32.8–35.0 mL and are not monotonically ordered; I therefore weaken the earlier suggestion of a general opposing completion trend. The m28 low-amount 1/1 result likewise makes amount dependence more plausible than a shared boundary reversal. The new m184 100-uL pure-EA result falls below both neighboring amounts, increasing the value of a repeat over another ordinary adjacent-ratio measurement. The m72 protocol pair differed at low amount, whereas the measured 2/1 pair was similar; this supports testing context dependence without assigning the difference solely to solvent identity. The m118 acquisition-time V2 underprediction of 29.00 mL is the strongest new failure, but nearby observations are too irregular to justify a broad upward correction. Pure-EA m182 remained broad at high amount, while m214 and m69 remained relatively early, further weakening universal aromatic-tail corrections. Recent m86 and amino-nitrile interior predictions were reasonably close, reducing the priority of more neighboring rows there. All error statements refer to acquisition-time predictions, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch turns recent failures into local experiments with interpretable alternatives. The m4 ratio and amount measurements, m118 boundary pair, and m182/m131/m214 contrasts target completion failures while preserving graph-specific counterexamples. Amount experiments span basic, neutral and acidic environments because the supplied observations support different onset and completion associations across those contexts. The m123 triplet and anisole anchor explore a predicted response maximum in neutral ether chemistry, extending coverage beyond the latest high-error molecules. Methoxy-carbonyl and alcohol comparisons test structural transfer in regions that connect early elution to later retention growth. Three repeats have specific roles: m72 assesses a new low-amount/protocol result, m184 tests a dip between neighboring amounts, and m81 assesses a short interval before interpreting adjacent-ratio curvature. Other duplicate candidate tuples are avoided. Several labels are expected to be ordinary; their value is to constrain where a correction should stop. The numerous zero V2 q10 values and some crossed V1 quantiles make interval widths unsuitable as a primary acquisition ranking in this packet. This design should improve conditional V1/V2 relationships and generalization across the Row-distribution without pursuing large elution volumes or better chromatographic performance. Unrecorded variables and within-tuple variation remain possible explanations where the local relationships do not reproduce.
